source: NCERT Class VIII, Social and Political Life III, Polity Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Why a Constitution
points: A **Constitution** is the **supreme/fundamental law** that lays down the rules by which a country is governed.
It defines the **structure and powers of government**, and the **rights and duties of citizens**.
It **limits the power of government** so that it cannot become tyrannical, and protects the rights of minorities.
India's Constitution came into force on **26 January 1950**.

sections.heading: 2. Making of the Constitution
points: Framed by the **Constituent Assembly (1946–1949)**; **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** chaired the **Drafting Committee**.
**Dr Rajendra Prasad** was the President of the Constituent Assembly.
It drew on the freedom struggle's ideals of **liberty, equality, justice and fraternity** and the sacrifices of many.

sections.heading: 3. Key Features of the Indian Constitution
points: **Federalism** — government at more than one level (Union, State, and local).
**Parliamentary form of government** — representatives elected by the people; universal adult franchise.
**Separation of powers** — three organs: **Legislature, Executive, Judiciary** — each checks the others.
**Fundamental Rights** — protect citizens against misuse of state power (right to equality, freedom, against exploitation, religion, culture/education, constitutional remedies).
**Secularism** — the state has no official religion and treats all religions equally.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Constitution = supreme law; defines government + rights/duties; limits state power.
Constituent Assembly (1946–49); Ambedkar = Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad = President.
In force 26 January 1950.
Key features: federalism, parliamentary government, separation of powers, fundamental rights, secularism.
Three organs: Legislature, Executive, Judiciary (checks & balances).

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Ambedkar** chaired the **Drafting Committee**; **Rajendra Prasad** was **President of the Constituent Assembly**.
The Constitution **came into force on 26 January 1950** (adopted 26 Nov 1949).
**Separation of powers** = Legislature, Executive, Judiciary — each limits the others.
**Secularism** (Indian) = no state religion + equal treatment of all faiths.
